name: Measured Casimir force between plates (Lamoreaux 1997; Mohideen-Roy 1998; Bressi 2002) and the ideal-plate energy E/A = -pi^2 hbar c/(720 d^3)

source.located: Mohideen & Roy, PRL 81, 4549 (1998) = arXiv:physics/9805038v2; Bressi, Carugno, Onofrio, Ruoso, PRL 88, 041804 (2002) = arXiv:quant-ph/0203002v1; Lamoreaux, PRL 78, 5 (1997) + erratum PRL 81, 5475 (1998) -- no arXiv copy; ideal-plate E/A and F/A as derived in Bordag, Mohideen, Mostepanenko, Phys. Rep. 353, 1 (2001) = arXiv:quant-ph/0106045 eqs (2.36),(2.37),(4.31); Brown-Maclay tensor (Phys. Rev. 184, 1272 (1969)) restated in Sopova & Ford arXiv:quant-ph/0204125 eq (52)

published_statement: Mohideen-Roy (physics/9805038 abstract, p.9): AFM measurement of the force between a metallized (Al + <20 nm Au/Pd) sphere of diameter 196 um and a flat plate, separations 0.1-0.9 um; 'consistent with present theoretical calculations including the finite conductivity, roughness and temperature corrections'; rms deviation 1.6 pN = 1% at the smallest separation; the ideal formula without corrections gives 6.3 pN (5% at the smallest separation). Theory compared via F0(d) = -pi^3 hbar c R/(360 d^3) (proximity force). Bressi et al. (quant-ph/0203002 abstract, eq. 4): force between chromium-coated parallel silicon surfaces via frequency shift of a cantilever, 0.5-3.0 um, K_C = (1.22 +- 0.18)e-27 N m^2 against Casimir's pi h c/480 = 1.3e-27 N m^2, '15% precision'. Lamoreaux 1997 (via Bordag et al. pp.209-210, 249): torsion pendulum, Au-over-Cu coated lens (R reported 11.3 cm, corrected to 12.5 cm in the 1998 erratum) and plate, 0.6-6 um, agreement 'at 5%' with the ideal sphere-plate formula; the erratum adds a 22% (Au) / 11% (Cu) finite-conductivity correction at 0.6 um and a +10.6% radius correction; Bordag et al.: '(5-10)% accuracy would probably apply at the smallest separations only', temperature corrections 'remain unconfirmed'. Ideal plates (Bordag et al. eq. 2.36-2.37, 4.31): E/A = -pi^2 hbar c/(720 a^3), F/A = -pi^2 hbar c/(240 a^4), for perfect conductors (eps -> infinity for all frequencies) at T = 0.
published_hypotheses: Measured quantity is a FORCE (Mohideen-Roy, Lamoreaux: sphere-plate force; Bressi: plate-plate force gradient via cantilever frequency shift) -- never an energy density or a stress tensor
Real metals: Al + Au/Pd (Mohideen-Roy), Cr (Bressi), Cu + Au (Lamoreaux); agreement at the 1% level required finite-conductivity and roughness corrections (Mohideen-Roy eqs 2-4)
Sphere-plate results compared through the proximity force approximation F = 2 pi R E/A(d), R >> d (Mohideen-Roy eq. 1; Bordag et al. eq. 4.106); only Bressi is plate-plate
Separation ranges: 0.1-0.9 um (Mohideen-Roy; absolute separations >=120 nm), 0.5-3.0 um (Bressi), 0.6-6 um (Lamoreaux)

Electrostatic backgrounds subtracted by calibration fits (residual potential 29 mV Mohideen-Roy; V0 = -68.6 mV Bressi; in Lamoreaux the electrostatic force was ~5x the Casimir force and d0 fitted to the expected Casimir force -- Mohideen-Roy p.3, Bordag et al. p.210)
Room temperature; thermal correction negligible at a << hbar c/(kT) and unconfirmed by Lamoreaux at 4-6 um
Ideal-plate formula: perfect conductors, flat infinite parallel plates, T = 0, zeta/cutoff-renormalised mode sum (Bordag et al. 2.33-2.36)

Uniform negative energy density -pi^2 hbar c/(720 a^4) between plates (Brown-Maclay, restated Sopova-Ford eq. 52) holds for perfect conductors only; for dispersive plates the gap energy density has an added positive position-dependent term (Sopova-Ford eq. 50)
hypothesis_drift: candidates.py:73-74 ADDS 'measured in the laboratory' to the ideal-plate ENERGY DENSITY rho = -pi^2 hbar c/(720 d^4). The sources measure a force between real metals; Sopova & Ford quant-ph/0204125 p.15: 'The existence of an attractive Casimir force is not an indicator of whether the energy density at the center of the plates is actually negative or not', and p.16: 'no clear way has been found to directly observe the local energy density'. Strengthening beyond the source.

tolman.py:483-485 ('the exact ISOTROPIC AVERAGE of the measured parallel-plate Casimir tensor') ADDS 'measured' to the TENSOR. Only the normal stress's effect (the force) is measured; rho and p_t are theory (Brown-Maclay, NAMED-NOT-READ). tolman.py:1317-1322 and 2539-2540 state it correctly ('whose FORCE is the one MEASURED quantity'; u_0 DERIVED) -- the drift is local to the prose at 483-485 and to candidates.py.

tolman.py:506-507 and 2855 (d, R = 1e-8, 1e-3) DROP the separation range: every cited measurement is at d >= 0.1 um (0.5 um for the only plate-plate one); the control is evaluated at d = 10 nm, a factor 10 below Mohideen-Roy's closest point and 50 below Bressi's, and below the gold skin depth c/omega_p = 21.93 nm that the tree itself banks (tolman.py:1508-1512, 3044). The MEASURED status of the force does not extend to 10 nm.

tolman.py:1317-1322 NAMES 'ideal parallel conducting plates' (hypothesis kept, honest) but DROPS that the measurements confirm Lifshitz theory with finite-conductivity corrections, not the ideal formula at the quoted precision: Mohideen-Roy p.9, ideal formula rms 6.3 pN vs 1.6 pN corrected. The 'MEASURED' label certifies real-plate forces; the ideal formula is their omega_p -> infinity / d >> lambda_p limit (computed here: eta(1 um) = 0.919, eta(100 nm) = 0.525, eta(10 nm) = 0.110 for plasma-model gold).
tolman.py:1317-1322, 2539-2540 DROP the proximity-force step: two of the three cited experiments (Lamoreaux, Mohideen-Roy) are sphere-plate and reach E/A only through PFA F = 2 pi R E/A.

tolman.py:1320, 2540 cite 'Lamoreaux 1997' without its erratum PRL 81, 5475 (1998) (lens radius 11.3 -> 12.5 cm, +10.6% in theory; 22% Au conductivity correction at 0.6 um), and without the later assessment that the 5% figure holds only at the smallest separations (Bordag et al. p.210). A citation discrepancy, recorded; it does not refute the force's existence or sign.

tolman.py:1325-1331 (plate_cell) assumes rho = -u_0 UNIFORM across the gap; that is Brown-Maclay's perfect-conductor result. For plasma-model plates Sopova-Ford eq. (50) adds a positive z-dependent term; computed here at the tree's d = 10 nm for gold (omega_p a = 0.456) the gap-centre energy density is POSITIVE, a^4 U = +0.0405 against the ideal -0.0137. The tree names 'ideal parallel conducting plates', so this is a hypothesis the tree keeps but does not flag as failing at its chosen d.
Temperature: dropped by the tree; immaterial at 10 nm (xi = 2 pi kT d/(hc) = 1.3e-3, Mohideen-Roy p.4 formula) -- no effect on the use.

rederivation.outcome: ALL ASSERTIONS PASS. (A, sympy) E/A = -pi^2 hbar c/(720 d^3) from Bordag et al. (2.36) with the Bose integral Gamma(4)zeta(4) = pi^4/15 (numerically confirmed; sympy cannot close the integral itself); F/A = -d(E/A)/dd = -3u_0 = -pi^2 hbar c/(240 d^4); tensor (-u0,-3u0,+u0) traceless; isotropic average p = -u0/3; raw-cell factor 9; u_0(10 nm) = 4.33375e4 J/m^3, m(R = 1 mm) = -2.019814e-21 kg -- the tree's numbers reproduce. (B) Bressi K_C theory = 1.30013e-27 N m^2 = pi^2 hbar c/240; measured 1.22 +- 0.18 -> pull -0.45 sigma; Lamoreaux radius correction +10.6%. (C, numeric) zero-T plasma-model Lifshitz eta(d) for gold: 0.110 at 10 nm, 0.525 at 100 nm, 0.871 at 600 nm (Lambrecht-Reynaud's optical-data 0.87), 0.986 at 6 um; nonretarded limit check 0.99994. (D, numeric) Sopova-Ford eq. (50): perfect-conductor limit recovered (1% at omega_p a = 1e4), sign change between omega_p a = 90 and 99 (paper: ~99); at gold 10 nm the gap-centre energy density is POSITIVE (+0.0405/a^4). Output log: rederive/casimir-force-measurements.out

later_literature.what: Local energy density between dispersive (plasma-model) half-spaces = negative constant Casimir term + positive position-dependent term; negative at the gap centre only for omega_p a > ~99 (a > 1.3 um for Al); the force's sign does not fix the energy density's sign; local energy density not directly observable. Reproduced numerically here.

Ideal formulas derived (2.36-2.37, 4.31); nonretarded Hamaker regime at a << lambda_0 (4.27); finite-conductivity corrections 10-20% at ~1 um; perturbation theory valid for a >= lambda_p; Lamoreaux 1997 erratum and '(5-10)% accuracy at the smallest separations only'; Harris-Chen-Mohideen 2000 extended to 62-350 nm at ~1%.

Au and Cu give equal forces within 1% over 0.6-6 um; eta_Au(0.6 um) = 0.87 vs Lamoreaux erratum's 0.78 -- resolves the Au/Cu discrepancy in Lamoreaux's comparison; 'more work is needed ... to reach an accurate agreement'.

Sphere-plate Au force 0.2-8 um; Drude-model extrapolation excluded at 95% CL over 0.2-4.8 um, plasma model consistent; physical explanation lacking. Confirms the force and the Lifshitz framework, contests the material model at finite T.
Continuing Drude/plasma debate for evanescent TE waves and magnetic metals; bears on finite-T real-metal forces at 0.1-few um, not on the ideal formula or 10 nm.

lacked_data: What the authors lacked: Lamoreaux 1997 lacked accurate optical data for the finite-conductivity correction and the correct lens radius (erratum 1998: +10.6% radius, 22% Au correction); Au-vs-Cu was later shown irrelevant (quant-ph/9912085), so his agreement claim was partly fortuitous (Mohideen-Roy p.3: corrections >20% 'not observed', electrostatic force 5x Casimir). Mohideen-Roy lacked later-precision patch-potential and PFA-beyond characterisation; Bressi lacked a model of the 1-2 um residual (Fig. 4 caption). Later data (Harris-Chen-Mohideen 2000 at 62-350 nm, Bimonte et al. 2021 at 0.2-8 um) CONFIRMED the force and the Lifshitz theory it tests, narrowed the precision claims, and opened the Drude/plasma question at finite T. Having it does NOT change the conclusion the tree needs from these papers -- an attractive force exists and matches E/A = -pi^2 hbar c/(720 d^3) in the limit d >> lambda_p. The data that change the tree's use were never lacking by these authors: no cited experiment measured at 10 nm, and no experiment measures an energy density. At the tree's d = 10 nm the real-gold E/A is 0.110 of ideal (computed) and the plasma-model gap-centre energy density is positive (Sopova-Ford 2002, reproduced). Evidence against M's hypothesis for this result: the ideal-plate derivation re-derives exactly and the three measurements agree with theory within their stated (corrected) errors; evidence for it, narrowly: Lamoreaux's 5% was overstated for want of data, a discrepancy, not a refutation.
grade_evidence: The published results stand as published: the ideal formula re-derives (sympy, exact), Bressi's plate-plate coefficient agrees with pi h c/480 at -0.45 sigma, Mohideen-Roy agree with corrected Lifshitz theory at 1%, and later work (Bimonte et al. 2021) confirms the force. No refuting counterexample exists. The tree's use is NARROWER than it states in three places: (1) candidates.py:73-74 and tolman.py:483-485 carry 'measured' onto the energy density / tensor, which no experiment measures (Sopova-Ford p.15-16); (2) tolman.py:506-507, 2855 evaluate at d = 10 nm, outside every cited range (>= 0.1 um) and below gold's skin depth, where real-gold E/A is 0.110 of ideal and the plasma-model gap-centre energy density is POSITIVE (+0.0405/a^4, computed); (3) the Lamoreaux citation omits its 1998 erratum. The tree NAMES 'ideal parallel conducting plates' at tolman.py:1317-1322, so the positive control's VERDICT YES -- which depends only on the sign of p_r of an ideal-plate construction and is already granted only 'test_field_background' -- is not moved. What is moved is the provenance claim ('measured', 'not an invention') at d = 10 nm and the magnitude m = -2.019814e-21 kg, which is an ideal-plate construction and not a measured-regime number.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree restricts 'MEASURED' to the force between real plates at d >= ~0.1 um (0.5 um plate-plate), labels u_0 and the tensor as ideal-plate constructions at d = 10 nm, and cites the Lamoreaux erratum -- or chooses d within the measured range and d >> c/omega_p. To DATA-DEPENDENT: if the positive control's verdict or a load-bearing magnitude were made to depend on real-metal E/A at 10 nm (then the Drude/plasma/optical-data choice and Hamaker constant would be live inputs). To WRONG: only a measurement contradicting the attractive force's sign or the d^-4 plate-plate law in the measured range; none was found. A direct measurement of the plate-plate force at ~10 nm would replace the plasma-model eta(10 nm) = 0.110 used here as evidence.
